final_result.validation_summary:
The caption accurately describes the image of Bernie Sanders speaking at the 2016 Democratic National Convention, as supported by the image check result. Viewers would not be misled about the image content based on the caption provided in this context .However, the image content does not appear in the article that accompanies this image, it can be considered a form of clickbait. That does not impact the outcome here because we are only assessing whether the caption is representative of the image content, and it is deemed to be so by the image check result with a high degree of confidence. As a result the OOC is set to false, as this image is not Out of Context in this scenario/task based on the results of the image check process. (Even if the broader article content doesn't connect to the image.)

NOTE: If the article were about the photo or related, it would score OOC = False with an even higher confidence score 10/10, if the article doesn't mention any Bernie Sanders then it would score OOC = True and the explanation would have to reflect the difference, which is an issue of context, but that goes beyond the current task.)

It could be possible that Bernie Sanders name is only mentioned once in the article, but it would still return OOC = False because the task is only checking whether the image is representative of the caption and not representative of the article as a whole, it does not check for clickbait, so as long as the caption mentions the image, and the image is representative of what the caption mentions, it returns a score of OOC = False. In many cases that is a valid outcome because the article might mention the reason for using that image in some tangential fashion. The presence of an image of Bernie Sanders (who may be indirectly related to DNC, the contents of the article) and the caption that calls it out leads to a verdict that is OOC = False by the image check and is very accurate and helpful in reducing bad outcomes overall in image verification tasks that focus only on caption-to-image verification. In the context of tasks or scenarios where verification requires broader context (or even a broader scan of the whole website or even looking at the search engine results of the site that has the image displayed), the image check becomes less useful or not useful at all and in that case it is better to rely solely on manual assessment of image-to-content validation with all the factors mentioned above as guidelines to determine the overall accuracy.


Also, it must be recognized that the image is being displayed in the context of this task, along with the caption, and the goal is to determine the truthfulness of the statement that the image IS an accurate representation of the caption, it cannot be determined what role the image would play in the content without looking at the original source. Since this is not the task, no attempts will be made to do so here and the focus will be on the representation of the caption itself, and if that is truthful based on the provided image only, that is the task that is intended and that is to be executed here in this case and in all cases.

Image-to-caption verification is a distinct task than Image-to-content verification which would need to be assessed in manual way with other verification frameworks and best practices that deal with issues such as clickbait and deceptive use of images and AI in media. In this case, the confidence score of 10 accurately reflects that, because it is not known whether in the broader context the image has been used to drive clicks, however the image and caption do confirm the validity of that statement regardless of what kind of clickbait may or may not have been attempted. Since the truth of the statements of the caption are validated by the image with a high degree of confidence, that is what the image check returns. The image and caption relationship and match and truthfulness is very accurately assessed with this image check and it should be recognized for these tasks (although it is less useful when more advanced questions need to be answered that require more contextual awareness of broader web pages and/or search engine results). 


The outcome would also be the same whether it is using advanced AI or manual review, because the task is very narrowly defined, but it is still a very useful and helpful task because there may be instances where the caption says the image of someone else and that is the most critical part of the evaluation to focus on in terms of usefulness and accuracy here. Any additional and secondary evaluations (such as is this a clickbait, or is this image actually used in the article) would go beyond the core objective of the validation here and need to be conducted outside of this task, as well as by other experts or systems that specialize in that kind of deception and manipulation that is not covered in the scope of this task.
